original.evidence: Plans/assistant-chat-design.md:24763 gives all four bindings: “Open target is `cmd.chat.open_investigation_target`”, “Export bundle is `cmd.chat.export_investigation_bundle`”, “Revoke item is `cmd.chat.revoke_investigation_item`”, “Open in Terminal is `cmd.terminal.open`”. Chat calls the old export and revoke IDs “retired source spellings: they are not commands, aliases or wiring rows, and nothing dispatches them.” It retires the old Open target spelling in the same paragraph. Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md:8633 lists “`cmd.chat.export_investigation_bundle`, `cmd.chat.revoke_investigation_item`”. Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md:22073 defines Open target as “A no-persist `navigation_wrapper`”. Plans/Wiring_Matrix.md:482–484 binds the same three IDs to their respective controls. Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md:18977 ties Open in Terminal to “the exact `terminal_session_id`”. Plans/assistant-chat-design.md:24769–24781 gives nine transition rows from creation through pause, resume, blocking, completion, failure and cancellation, including “`blocked` | `user_action_completed` | `running`” and “`blocked` | `cancel` | `cancelled`”. It requires a permitted cancellation on the current blocked episode and identifies the separate child-task and terminal state owners.
